entries.dictionary: 改訂新版 世界大百科事典
entries.heading: 僧 (そう)
entries.evidence: The returned opening explains the Buddhist renunciant/clergy reference and distinguishes the individual from the community sense. The Japan section describes several historically different clerical arrangements rather than one universal modern lifestyle.
entries.decision: Teach the ordinary Buddhist priest/monk sense, retaining the community sense in source dispositions. Do not equate every English priest with 僧, require every person so called to follow one lifestyle, or infer a new character reading from a compound.
entries.limits: The first 11000-character extraction was truncated within the long encyclopedic article; pagination at 11000 returned further concluding material. This is not a full read of every dictionary on the HTML page. No Daijisen or 字通 definition of 僧 was returned or claimed. Historical specifics are not needed for the planned teaching.

entries.dictionary: 精選版 日本国語大辞典; 改訂新版 世界大百科事典
entries.heading: そう‐りょ【僧侶】; 僧侶 (そうりょ)
entries.evidence: Nikkoku explicitly allows the religious group and an individual. The encyclopedia identifies the narrower Buddhist reference while acknowledging broader historical use for Christian clergy and cautioning about inappropriate cross-religion classifications.
entries.decision: Add only the necessary 僧侶 そうりょ support article, centred on its Buddhist noun sense. It can refer to an individual; 侶 does not force a plural translation or mean that the speaker is the monk's companion. Avoid an absolute never-used-outside-Buddhism rule.
entries.limits: Daijisen, 字通 and Nipponica sections returned attribution only; no definitions from them are claimed. The encyclopedia's historical breadth is not unrestricted modern interchangeability with 神父 or 牧師.

entries.heading: 侶 / 常用漢字 9画; 字音 リョ
entries.evidence: The actual heading supplies リョ; the semantic section gives companion/fellow meanings. Frozen KANJIDIC2 independently gives リョ, ロ and とも for this character.
entries.decision: The necessary support can explain 僧 ソウ plus 侶 リョ as a lexicalized Buddhist-clergy noun with a fellow/companion contribution, not derive its pronunciation by splitting kana alone. Keep 侶 in the word's metadata even though it has no card. No 侶 card or wider reading course is added in this batch.
entries.limits: The historical discussion contains gaiji images that were not inspected. No historical or phonetic derivation is needed or claimed; semantic 字訓 do not add readings to the frozen 僧 metadata.

entries.heading: ぼう‐さん〔バウ‐〕【坊さん】
entries.evidence: The first sense is a familiar, respectful designation for a monk; the second is a familiar designation for a boy. The first sense's synonym list includes 僧 and 僧侶.
entries.decision: Preserve the actual N2 坊さん article, primary reading and exclusions. Its religious sense overlaps the proposed new support; do not make them competing wrong answers merely because their register differs. Matching exact word titles can use existing exact-title deduplication rather than manufacturing a new semantic distinction.
entries.limits: Familiar respect is not a universal recommendation for ceremonial address. No new frequency ranking or blanket formal/informal substitution rule.
